explanation: The OK hand sign is understood positively in Italy, meaning 'fine,' 'perfect,' or agreement, with no vulgar connotation of the kind found in some neighboring Mediterranean countries. It's used comfortably in casual, dining, and business contexts alike.
local_tip: Use the OK sign naturally to confirm agreement or approval — it won't cause offense the way it might in Turkey or Brazil.
regional_note: In Naples it also has an old folk meaning: an upturned circle once symbolized love or marriage, a downturned one justice, though this is largely historical trivia today.

also_check.note: The OK sign is considered vulgar, resembling an obscene gesture.
It can be read as a homophobic insult or vulgar reference.
In the south it can mean 'zero' or 'worthless'; the positive 'OK' meaning is more common in the north.
